title: fix(react): a row cap the contract refuses is not "authored" in the shared gate (objectui#9899)
body:
Fixes #9899

`ElementDataSourceGate` decides, per key, whether a component's own value should suppress the one a bound saved view supplies. The `columns` branch has always decided that by **CONTENT** — an authored-but-empty list yields, because *"supplying the columns is the reason a view was named"*. The `limit` branch twenty lines below decided it by **PRESENCE**, so a value the contract refuses counted as authorship and the view's legitimate cap was never written.

## FIRST DELIVERABLE — the population measurement, before the rule

Taken on the branch base `dc4924655`, over `git ls-files` (8155 files): every strict-JSON file parsed and walked as a schema tree, every JSON fence in `.md`/`.mdx` parsed the same way, and a literal scan across `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs`. Usability predicate is objectui#9925's, restated: `typeof v === 'number' && Number.isInteger(v) && v > 0`.

| carrier | total found | CONTROL: legitimate | spec-refused | of those, bind a view |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| metadata `pagination.pageSize` | 9 | **9** | **0** | 0 |
| metadata flat `pageSize` | 16 | **16** | **0** | 0 |
| metadata flat `limit` | 11 | **11** | **0** | 0 |
| source literal `pagination.pageSize` | 108 | **97** | 11 | — |
| source literal flat `pageSize` | 186 | **173** | 13 | — |
| source literal flat `limit` | 126 | **116** | 10 | — |

**The control is LIT in every row** — a legitimate cap is found by each carrier, so a zero is a reading and not a dead instrument.

**The refused population is TEST-ONLY.** Every source-literal refusal sits in a `__tests__` file that exists to pin this very refusal (`ObjectGrid.pageSizeNonPositive-9853`, `ListView.pageSizeNonPositive-9897`, `record-reference-rail.rowLimitNonPositive-9925`, `RecordRelatedListRenderer.speclimit`, `query-params-closed-keys-7497`), or is an unrelated `limit: 0` in the ESLint rule corpus for `no-unprefixed-query-params`. One production hit — `RelatedList.tsx` — is the literal `0` inside `pageSize && pageSize > 0 ? pageSize : 0`, i.e. a guard, not authored metadata.

⇒ **zero authored nodes, zero published metadata, no victim.** Triage's re-grade switch (「若人口测出来非零且含已发布元数据」) does **not** fire, so the rule lands.

## What an author actually suffered — measured end to end, not inferred

A throwaway probe rendered the real `ListViewBlock` (real gate, real `ListView`, stub child grid) with a component carrying `pagination.pageSize: 0` under a view supplying `7`, and recorded what left on the wire and who said anything. The vitest root config aliases `@object-ui/react` to `packages/react/src`, so this reads the edited source with no `dist` hop.

| | `$top` on the wire | `ListView` diagnostic | gate diagnostic |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **before** | **100** (renderer default) | 1 | 0 |
| **after** | **7** (the view's cap) | 0 | 1 |

⚠️ **This corrects the relayed claim in the card.** Triage relayed 「component `0` + view `7` ⇒ 0, not 7」. That is true at the **gate's output key**, and the appended suite pins it there. It is **not** what reaches the query: objectui#9897's renderer guard already refuses the `0`, so `$top` was the renderer's own default `100`. The real harm is therefore the opposite of a starved read — **the named view's cap was dropped and the read went WIDER than the view asked for**, in the one direction a named view exists to prevent.

## The diagnostic question, decided on that evidence

The brief left open whether a **relay** owes a loud refusal at all. The measurement answers it: **before** this repair the author *was* being told, once, by `ListView`. **After** it, the gate substitutes a usable cap, that renderer correctly sees nothing to report, and its message goes silent — so **the repair removes the only place the author was being told**. Staying quiet would have been exactly the refused outcome (「让它悄悄传下去但换个默认值」), just one layer up.

⇒ **the gate emits it**, once per declaration, from an effect (never from render), on the same `console.warn` channel the renderer sites use, naming the refused value, the key it was written on, and the cap used instead. Exactly one message before and after — the layer that makes the decision is the layer that reports it. Two silence controls pin that it says nothing when no cap was authored, and nothing when the view supplies no cap to displace with (there the value stays and the renderer's own message is still the one that fires).

## The predicate

A deliberate **local restatement** of objectui#9925's `isUsableRowLimit`. ⛔ Not imported and ⛔ not extracted to a shared helper — both are cross-package moves outside this fence. The cost is written into the comment rather than hidden.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/src/element-data-source/` — **42 passed**. 8 of them fail on the base commit (reproduction: `expected { pageSize: +0 } to deeply equal { pageSize: 7 }`, and the same for `-10` and `25.5`); every CONTROL in the new block passes **both** before and after, so a branch that simply stopped counting any authored cap could not pass it.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/` — **89 files, 1127 tests passed**.
- Consumers of the `limit` mapping: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/ packages/plugin-grid/ packages/plugin-kanban/ packages/plugin-timeline/` — **310 files, 3069 tests passed**.
- …and the remaining two of the six: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/ packages/plugin-form/` — **293 files, 2871 tests passed | 1 skipped**. (Added by the claiming seat at 2026-09-19T10:19Z, from the dev's report: the Tests section above predated this run, so all six limit-mapping consumers are now listed rather than four.)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check` — clean (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`), after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` supplied the dependency dists.
- `pnpm exec eslint .` (repo-wide, not narrowed) — **5159 files, 0 errors**; the two changed files carry 15 warnings, all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` / `react-refresh`, and this branch adds none.
- Gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` — all exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

Findings outside this card's fence, recorded rather than filed:

- **noted, not filed** — `packages/plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx` carries prose citing 「the gate's `readLimit(base) === undefined` branch」. That branch is now `!isUsableRowLimit(...)`, so the quoted spelling has drifted. Its *argument* survives unchanged (a materialised default `limit` would still defeat the branch, because a default would be usable). Out of fence: `packages/plugin-kanban`. Successor: whoever next edits that file's header — the opportunistic-repair rule, not a sweep.
- **noted, not filed** — `savedViewLimit` in `packages/core` reads a saved view's `pagination.pageSize` with no usability check, so a *view* carrying a refused cap composes into `composed.limit` and is written onto the component key. Unchanged by this PR and explicitly a different card (the brief fences `packages/core` out). Successor: the `savedViewLimit` card.
- **noted, not filed** — the `object-grid` props face declares its own `pagination` key `z.unknown()` and the flat `pageSize` shorthand a bare `z.number()`, so a component-level `pagination.pageSize: 0` is **not** refused at that face. The refusal this change rests on is the pagination CONFIG contract plus the flat `limit` the value is lowered into. Recorded because the card's wording (「a value the spec REFUSES」) reads as if the component face refuses it, and it does not. Successor: none identified — stated here so the next reader of the branch is not misled.
